newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Westpac Australia April leading index rises.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Westpac Australia April leading index rises.

text.p: The Westpac-Melbourne Institute Leading index of Australian economic activity, which measures where activity will be in six to nine months time, rose 2.9 points or 1.8 percent in April, lifting the annual growth rate to 6.2 percent from 2.8 percent.
The coincident index, which provides a broad measure of the current state of economic activity, fell 0.5 points or 0.4 percent in April.
The leading index of inflation rose slightly to 4.4 percent in April from 4.3 percent in March.
Westpac chief economist Nigel Stapledon said the weakness in the coincident index, which is now running well below trend, was a broad measure of the current weak state of the economy.

"The economy has been performing well below its potential over the past year," Stapledon said in a commentary. "Full time jobs have actually contracted slightly versus trend potential growth of closer to 1.5 per annum and correspondingly the unemployment rate has continued to edge higher," he said.
The rise in the leading index more than reverses the one percent fall in the index in March.

"The aggregate picture is that the leading index has lifted from below to about trend, which suggests that by late 1997 economic activity will be running much closer to its potential than is presently the case," Stapledon said.
He said a fair period of above-trend economic growth above four percent was needed to reverse the rise in unemployment, which was 8.8 percent in May.

"The Reserve Bank's decision to cut interest rates in May has increased the probability of four percent plus growth emerging in 1998 but, for any degree of comfort, we would need to see consistently strong signals from the leading index over
the next several months," Stapledon said.
"If not, then the Reserve Bank will find itself under pressure to again push interest rates lower to help ensure that stronger growth does emerge in 1998," he said.
